content.title: How Rory McIlroy won Masters 2026 to become fourth man to defend title
content.text: McIlroy held off challenges from Cameron Young, Justin Rose and Scottie Scheffler to go back-to-back at Augusta NationalRory McIlroy has won the Masters for the second straight year Getty ImagesMcIlroy wins second straight MastersRory McIlroy has won the Masters for the second straight year, shooting a final-round 71 to finish at 12 under par, one stroke better than runner-up Scottie Scheffler. A dramatic final round saw Cameron Young, who began the day with a share of the lead, and Justin Rose both lead by two strokes at separate points, but neither could keep pace on the back nine. McIlroy is just the fourth golfer to win back-to-back Masters tournaments, joining Jack Nicklaus (1965-66), Nick Faldo (1989-90) and Tiger Woods (2001-02). This is the sixth major championship for the golfer from Northern Ireland. Share your reaction with us at live@theathletic.com. WinnerPOSPLAYERTOTAL1Rory McIlroyNIR-12SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementCan McIlroy get to 10 majors? Getty ImagesThis Q&A from our Alex Kirshner and Gabby Herzig is part of our Golf Briefing newsletter on Rory McIlroy's win at the Masters:Alex: That's six majors and two green jackets. He's won a road Ryder Cup. The Grand Slam was already in the bag. I don't sense that Rory will ever have a complacency problem, but how would you even judge success for him over the next, say, five years of his career? Gabby: McIlroy just talked about this in his news conference. It sounds like he originally thought that winning the Grand Slam would provide him the ultimate satisfaction, but it didn’t. And I interpret that to mean that McIlroy is about to put his foot on the gas in majors. I’d dare to say that McIlroy is chasing double digits in his major count. Maybe that won’t happen in the next five or six years, but it doesn’t feel out of the question at all for McIlroy’s career as a whole.Which shot stands out? Getty ImagesThis Q&A from our Alex Kirshner and Gabby Herzig is part of our Golf Briefing newsletter on Rory McIlroy's win at the Masters:Alex: You watched perhaps thousands of golf shots. Which one that you saw in person will stick with you the longest?Gabby: Honestly, this sounds counterintuitive, but I think the two out-of-sorts golf shots I saw McIlroy hit on both No. 11 and No. 12 with irons yesterday will stick with me the most from this tournament. For years, McIlroy has been telling the media that he will really know that he’s reached elite levels of the game if he is able to win tournaments without his best stuff. And this week, he did not have that — especially off the tee. Even after Sunday’s round, where he started to swing a little bit more freely, McIlroy was ranked No. 53 out of 54 in driving accuracy for the entire week, and he still won the Masters. It’s an absurd statement, especially knowing that the strength of McIlroy’s game are his tee shots. His gritty short game and putting held things up for him all week, and it paid off.During his winner’s news conference, I actually asked him to grade his play: He gave his driving a B-, his irons a B and his short game and putting an A+.How was this year different? Getty ImagesThis Q&A from our Alex Kirshner and Gabby Herzig is part of our Golf Briefing newsletter on Rory McIlroy's win at the Masters:Alex: To what extent did watching McIlroy this week feel different than watching him here every other year? Was the crowd more receptive to someone else winning? Were you more confident that he wouldn't let this thing get away from him?Gabby: It felt different, because the stakes objectively weren’t as high for him. He wasn’t chasing that one last win, he no longer “needed” the career Grand Slam. So he could breathe. Even after he let a six-shot 36-hole lead disappear, there was less on the line. You could see how that impacted him from a confidence standpoint, and other players took note of it. Freddie Couples even said, “Rory might never lose this things again.”But that did not mean his actual golf was any less stressful to watch. I was out there as the crowds swung with emotion yesterday. McIlroy is so human and so relatable in the way that you never know he’s going to do next. There were definitely a few people out there rooting for Justin Rose, but generally, McIlroy is the crowd pleaser because he makes things entertaining in a beautiful way.How sportsbooks reacted to McIlroy's win Multiple sportsbooks were happy with Rory McIlroy winning the 2026 Masters. Before the event began, McIlroy's odds to win his second green jacket were in the range of 11-1 to 14-1, depending on the sportsbook."Rory [McIlroy] was a very good result for the book as support for him was tempered pre-tournament," VP of risk management at the Westgate Sportsbook, Jeff Sherman, told The Athletic.Borgata Sportsbook director Thomas Gable shared similar sentiments, 💬 "Rory (McIlroy) winning that green jacket was the best outcome for us in terms of the pre-tournament outright winner market."McIlroy makes more history Getty ImagesRory McIlroy made history for the second straight year at Augusta National. Last year, it was earning the career Grand Slam. This year, it's becoming the fourth player to repeat as the Masters champion.Our Gabby Herzig has the story on McIlroy's win here. SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementAggressive mindset pays off Rory McIlroy said he got defensive last year on the 13th hole in the final round, and that hurt him. He said he stayed aggressive today on the 12th and 13th holes because of what happened last year.💬“Staying aggressive and staying committed, especially on those two holes, served me.”Let's hear from Scottie Scheffler After shooting a final-round 68, Scottie Scheffler spoke with CBS despite losing by one. 💬 “The first few days. I played what I was really solid on Thursday. Friday with the softer greens. That round really hurt.”“Over the weekend, I put up a good fight to give myself a chance. Just finished a couple shots shot.”Georgia natives to win the Masters Russell Henley got close today and likely had a real chance to win the Masters as a Georgia native. But the fact remains the same: Only three Georgia natives have won the Masters: Claude Harmon (Savannah, 1948), Tommy Aaron (Gainesville, 1973) and Larry Mize (Augusta, 1987).Another 'stinger' for Rose Justin Rose finished in the top 10 at the Masters for the eighth time, and that includes three runner-up finishes. He finished T3 this year at 10 under.And he received a terrific ovation from the spectators surrounding the 18th green.💬 “It was nice. I felt like the crowd was amazing to me all week long. They pulled for me all week long. I felt their encouragement and support. At the end, it kind of goes a little flat. It's more of a sympathy than anything.“But it was still, nonetheless, very beautiful. It’s another little stinger.”Schauffele is 'playing pretty nice' Xander Schauffele’s 2025 season was thrown off by a rib injury, but it seems like he is back to being himself health-wise. And his game has followed. Schauffele finished at 8 under and is tied for ninth.💬 “I feel like I played better than what I shot. Sometimes that's how golf goes. You need a few things to go your way, a few lip-out putts to lip in. But for the most part, I felt like I controlled my ball and wasn't in too many weird spots. Just struggled on the greens a little bit overall.“I've got something good coming around the corner here. I'm playing pretty nice.”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementNot looking for chatter Getty ImagesA year ago Bryson DeChambeau was quite bothered by the lack of chatter between he and Rory McIlroy in the final group at the Masters. Cameron Young was ready for it and typical of his laid-back personality, not offended by it.“I mean, I'm not one to talk a ton to begin with, and I don't think he really be the wanted to talk to me today. Sunday at the Masters in the final group, you know, don't wish anything poorly on the guy, but we're playing against each other,” Young said. “Not trying to be best friends out there.“Just one of those times that either you leave each other be and if there is a moment — there were one or two but not many.”Young shot a 73 today to finish at 10 under par, in a four-way tie for third. It’s his best-ever finish at the Masters but still came up short of his hope for the day.“If you go through the back nine I pretty much had a birdie chance on every hole and didn't make any. That's how it goes sometimes,” Young said.Some crystal and a strong finish for Hatton Tyrrell Hatton shot his second 6-under 66 for the week today and finished at 10 under for his second top-10 Masters finish. He had an eagle and six birdies in the final round, including four straight birdies on the second nine.💬 “I'm really happy with the round that I put together in the end. Obviously, I had a nice run on the back nine.”The eagle came on the seventh hole when he holed out from the fairway with his approach. Players who score an eagle during the week receive a crystal prize from the club.💬 “The first thing is I shouted, crystal, which, yeah, obviously happy to make eagle. That's a huge bonus in the round, and, it helped me get a little bit of momentum.”Henley misses opportunities for more Russell Henley finished with six straight pars today, but he missed his chances on the green to claim his first major. The Georgia native finished at 10 under after a 68 today for his second top-10 Masters finish.💬 “I hit it amazing today. I gave myself a bunch of looks. Unfortunately, I didn't capitalize on those looks on the back, like I would have liked to.“I felt like I handled the pressure well, handled the conditions well. It was tricky out there. I just hit it great. I’m really thankful for a good finish. I wish I would have made some more putts and got a little closer to the lead, but overall, I’m very thankful.”Young felt like he handled the pressure Cameron Young finished in the top 10 at the Masters for the third time today with a T3 finish at 10 under. He shot a 1-over 73 today in the final round while playing with winner Rory McIlroy.💬 “I think I handled it fine; I just didn't make anything. That's the story of the week, honestly if you look through all four rounds. I had a chip in yesterday and maybe made a putt or two over 10 feet, and really that was it.“So I feel like I played the golf I needed to. I just didn't have the day making anything at all.”Rahm on his week Jon Rahm, a former Masters champion, finished the week at 1 over after rounds of 78-70-73-68. So what does he take from the week?💬 “Today was much better. Crazy, same person, right? Even though I made some mistakes I was able to rectify quite a few of them and have a good round. “I'll say it again, a lot of what not to do. I played really bad the two days. Shot 2-under on the second round but that was about as good as I should have shot with how I was hitting it.”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementScheffler critiques Masters' Friday setup Scottie Scheffler made it quite clear after his round that he's pleased with the way he fought this weekend to give himself a chance, but disappointed at how Friday went for reasons in and out of his control.He was in the Thursday PM/Friday AM wave, shooting 70-74, and then watched Rory McIlroy shoot an afternoon 65 on Friday, and Cameron Young shoot a 67.💬 “I'm not in charge of course setup. I would have liked it to have been a little bit more equal in terms of the firmness on Thursday and Friday. I was a bit surprised at how soft things were on Friday afternoon, especially as it got late in the day.“But the weather also changes and it was a bit windy on Thursday, so who knows. That's part of the game.”Scottie was 12 back of McIlroy to start the weekend and ended up one shot back. “A pretty good run,” Scheffler said.Scheffler comes up just short Scottie Scheffler made a nice run this weekend in the Masters, but he couldn’t overcome the 74 he shot on Friday.Scheffler had rounds of 65-68 on the weekend, and had four birdies today. He finished second to Rory McIlroy, one shot back.💬 “The first two days I played what I felt was really solid on Thursday, and then Friday with the softer greens, that round really hurt, especially mistakes I made on the back nine. But overall over the weekend, I put up a good fight, did a lot of good stuff in order to give myself a chance and ultimately came up short.”McIlroy nets record prize money Not only does Rory McIlroy have another green jacket to slip into and another trophy for the mantlepiece, he also walks away with the biggest prize packet in major-championship history.Today's victory has earned him $4.5million in prize money, while second-placed Scottie Scheffler will pocket $2.43m.The first-place prize ties the Players Championship as the most lucrative payout in golf.What has McIlroy learned? Getty ImagesWhat has this tournament taught Rory McIlroy?💬 “Good things come to those who wait, maybe. Just keep going. I found myself in a very similar position today where I was last year, two or three behind. But I just played solid golf after that.”And what about having his parents there with him after they stayed at home last year?“I caught myself out on the golf course today thinking about them and thought, ‘No, not yet.’ But it was really cool to have them here.”
